Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Markets coverage dominates the business press right now: a deepening AI-chip stock selloff collided with the start of big bank earnings season, while bond yields climbed to multi-decade highs on deficit and inflation worries. Geopolitical shocks — Houthi attacks disrupting Saudi Arabia, a contested US-Russia diesel deal, and simmering Iran tensions — are also rippling through energy markets and corporate travel plans.

stories.headline: AI-chip selloff deepens as Broadcom CEO warns of 'casino' mentality
stories.summary: A selloff in chipmakers intensified on fears about the sustainability of the AI trade just as Wall Street banks kicked off earnings season, pulling major indexes lower even as some other sectors gained. A selloff in chipmakers deepened on concerns about the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence trade, putting pressure on equity markets as Wall Street banks kicked off the earnings season. Asian markets bore the brunt, with shares of South Korean memory chip makers SK Hynix and Samsung dropping 10.1% and 7.4%, respectively, on Tuesday, pulling the country's benchmark Kospi index down more than 5.4%.

stories.headline: Big banks report mixed Q3 earnings as JPMorgan misses, Goldman beats
stories.summary: JPMorgan posted surprisingly weak third-quarter results while Goldman Sachs and Citigroup beat expectations, reflecting a choppy trading environment and the bite of rising interest rates. Forbes reported that JPMorgan Chase posted roughly $27.04 billion in net interest income, though it missed analyst expectations for revenues and net income, while Goldman Sachs recorded a 72% year-over-year surge in equities revenue, reaching $6.44 billion, with investment banking fees also climbing.

stories.headline: Rising bond yields signal deepening deficit anxiety
stories.summary: Analysts say investors are demanding a bigger premium to hold government debt, a shift some see as a troubling signal about mounting US debt and deficits. FT separately reported that bond funds are seeing unusually strong demand even amid the rout, as yields hit multi-decade highs.

stories.headline: Houthi pressure on Saudi Arabia disrupts airlines and rattles oil markets
stories.summary: Attacks tied to Iran-backed militants are squeezing Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's economy, forcing Delta to delay its planned first-ever nonstop US-Saudi route until March and prompting an FAA safety warning for airlines flying over the kingdom.

stories.headline: Trump's Russian diesel deal draws bipartisan fire in Congress
stories.summary: Moderate Republicans joined Democrats in criticizing the administration's agreement with Putin to temporarily ease sanctions and release Russian diesel to global markets to curb fuel prices.

stories.headline: White House pushes ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign over gift allegations
stories.summary: Trump had floated firing the US ambassador to Greece after reports she accepted improper gifts, and the White House has now asked her to step down.

Business.gaps: Puck had no business-relevant items in the feed or search; The Information's search results on AI chip deals were all older than the 48-hour window and not current news.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are converging on the U.S. permitting-reform fight in Congress, the fallout from rising power prices tied to data-center demand, and a wave of utility/grid consolidation and regulatory decisions (Dominion-NextEra, FERC-PJM). Geopolitics also intrudes, with a Trump-announced Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire and a Kazakhstan uranium deal favoring China drawing notice.

stories.headline: Huffman pushes back on Senate's bipartisan permitting deal
stories.summary: Rep. Jared Huffman, the top Democrat on the House Natural Resources Committee, is raising objections to the Senate's energy permitting bill, warning that developers could get paid off rather than actually approved when projects are blocked.

stories.headline: Trump declares an 'energy ceasefire' in the Russia-Ukraine war
stories.summary: The U.S. president announced an immediate halt to energy-related attacks between Russia and Ukraine, though it remains unclear whether this truce will hold any longer than a prior one he claimed to have brokered.

stories.headline: TotalEnergies buys up U.S. solar after axing its offshore wind projects
stories.summary: Despite taking over $1 billion from the Trump administration to cancel its offshore wind projects, TotalEnergies' joint venture with KKR is adding 700 megawatts of solar in Texas and Ohio in a $1.2 billion deal.

stories.headline: Dominion-NextEra merger hearing zeroes in on rates and data centers
stories.summary: A local hearing on the proposed Dominion-NextEra merger focused on how the deal would affect customer rates and data-center growth in Virginia.

stories.headline: FERC rejects most of PJM's plan to curtail large data-center loads
stories.summary: Federal regulators found that PJM's proposal to curtail large loads lacking matching new generation intrudes on state jurisdiction and appears discriminatory.

stories.headline: How utilities lost their grip on Washington
stories.summary: A new analysis examines how utilities have seen their political influence erode in Washington amid the data-center power boom and shifting policy fights.

stories.headline: New coalition launches to help small U.S. towns lead on clean energy
stories.summary: A newly announced group aims to help small towns, which are often overlooked in clean-energy policy, gain more collective influence by banding together.

Energy.gaps: Argus Media could not be searched this session, so no recent coverage is reported for it. E&E News' own site stopped publishing new content after August 31 (it has folded into POLITICO Pro), so no fresh items could be verified beyond that transition. Reuters, FT, WSJ, NYT, and The Economist block web search and no feed items were provided for them, so their current coverage could not be assessed.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Africa-focused outlets are converging heavily on the Ethiopia-Eritrea/Tigray conflict escalation, alongside major business stories like Dangote's oversubscribed refinery IPO, Microsoft's retreat from its Nairobi engineering hub, and a swirl of debt, mining and governance stories from Zimbabwe, DRC, Morocco and Niger.

stories.headline: Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions escalate into open war fears over Tigray
stories.summary: With Ethiopian federal forces having retaken Mekelle from the TPLF, analysts are now scrutinizing Eritrea's military capacity amid fears of a broader war, as Asmara and Addis Ababa openly accuse each other of launching hostilities.

stories.headline: Former DRC president Kabila joins forces with Rwanda-backed M23
stories.summary: Joseph Kabila has taken a more direct role in the conflict by joining with the M23 armed group to head a new political-military outfit, deepening the crisis in eastern DRC.

stories.headline: Dangote keeps $49bn refinery IPO open past deadline
stories.summary: Although just over 3% of the Nigerian refinery is up for sale and already oversubscribed, the offer is being extended to 27 October to build a broader pan-African shareholder base rather than raise more cash.

stories.headline: Microsoft to close Nairobi engineering centre, hundreds of jobs at risk
stories.summary: The closure would unwind a flagship project premised on African engineers building globally competitive products without leaving the continent, a blow to Kenya's tech ambitions.

stories.headline: Sanctioned tycoon Tagwirei put in charge of Zimbabwe's investment push
stories.summary: President Mnangagwa's appointment of the US-sanctioned businessman Kudakwashe Tagwirei as economic development minister puts him in charge of selling Zimbabwe's investment case, raising questions about how foreign investors will respond.

stories.headline: Niger declares 'exceptional severity' environmental incident after oil blowout
stories.summary: Authorities confirmed a massive blowout of oil and gas in the country's eastern desert last month has caused a severe environmental crisis.

stories.headline: Morocco's PAM forms governing coalition after election win
stories.summary: New Prime Minister Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri has announced a coalition bringing together PAM, Istiqlal and other parties to form Morocco's next government.

stories.headline: African debt crisis deepens as IMF prepares World Economic Outlook
stories.summary: Ahead of the IMF's flagship outlook release in Bangkok, reporting suggests that behind a headline message of stability lies a sharper fight over mounting African debt burdens.

Africa.gaps: Mining Weekly and African Business block direct outlet-specific search confirmation of a single lead story for the latest 24-48 hours beyond general site listings (Anglo American's South Africa investment comments and the Top 100 Banks report are the most recent items found, dated slightly earlier than 24-48h). Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, WSJ, BBC provided no Africa-specific feed items in the supplied batch, so their Africa coverage could not be assessed this cycle.
